speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have sudden-onset vertigo; to better assess this, are you currently experiencing nausea, hearing loss, or tinnitus alongside the spinning sensation? Additionally, has this episode been triggered by changes in head position?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very short duration for the dizziness; have you noticed any difficulty walking, double vision, or slurred speech during those episodes? Also, does moving your head in any specific direction currently trigger the sensation again?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given the brief duration of your symptoms and the absence of neurological deficits like double vision or slurred speech, this fits the classic presentation of BPPV. We can confirm this with a bedside head-impulse test and the Dix-Hallpike maneuver.
